Dashboard templates
Starting layouts — a template is the arrangement only; it binds to your services when instantiated. Not the same asset as Settings → Templates (those are infrastructure shapes).
Golden Signals
Latency, errors, throughput, saturation per service — the SRE classic, wired to whatever you run.
8 widgetsUse layout
Release Review
Deploy markers, error delta before/after, rollback shortcut — for the hour after you ship.
6 widgetsUse layout
On-call Handoff
Firing alerts, open AI insights, DLQ depths, last 24 h anomalies — what the next person needs.
7 widgetsUse layout
Postgres Deep-dive
Connections, locks, slow queries, WAL, vacuum — one instance, everything that matters.
9 widgetsUse layout
Team Weekly
Cost trend, deploy count, incident minutes, SLO budgets — the manager view, honestly labeled.
6 widgetsUse layout
Instantiating never provisions anything — a dashboard reads, it doesn’t create. Personas differ; that’s the point of five layouts instead of one.

Scaling

Autoscale
A floor for reliability, a ceiling for cost, a signal in between.
Scale to zero

Range

7+ · policy

1 min

always on
Now · 3

this hour

worst case

Why two caches, not one bigger one
Different risk appetites deserve different instances: cache holds recomputable page fragments where eviction is free, while sessions holds carts where eviction logs users out. Separate instances mean separate memory pressure, separate eviction policies, and a flush on one never touches the other.

Valkey 7.2 · AI insights
production
Proposal · Switch eviction to allkeys-lru, raise maxmemoryAsk a follow-upprp_ca11e0 · awaiting your review
Evidence — what I read
memory used 1.9 GB of 2.0 GB (95%) · maxmemory-policy = noeviction
errors 3.1k OOM-command rejects/hr since 14:10 — writes failing, not evicting
keys hit rate 88% · session:* 61% · cart:* 22% · 40% of keys have no TTL
Reasoning
With noeviction and memory full, new writes are rejected (the OOM errors), not old keys dropped. session:* and cart:* are cache-safe to evict by LRU — the app treats a miss as a cold read. Raising maxmemory to 3 GB restores headroom; allkeys-lru ends the write failures.
Proposed change
- maxmemory-policy noeviction
+ maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
- maxmemory 2 GB
+ maxmemory 3 GB
Impact
write failures → 0 · hit rate ≈ unchanged · cost +$11/mo (2→3 GB)
Open in Settings (D14)Apply in staging firstDismiss (logged)Applied as you, via assistant — same permissions, same audit

Proposal · Lifecycle — expire temp uploads, tier cold originalsAsk a follow-upprp_st77a4 · awaiting your review
Evidence — what I read
size 48.1 GB · +2.3 GB/wk · $9/mo
age 31 GB not read in 30d · mostly uploads/tmp/*
access uploads/tmp/* write-once — 0 GETs after 48h · originals/* re-read weekly
Reasoning
uploads/tmp/* are written once and never read after two days — safe to expire at 7 days. 22 GB of originals/* older than 30 days are read rarely; moving them to infrequent-access cuts cost with only a first-read latency penalty. No deletes yet — these are rules you review.
Proposed change
rule 1 prefix uploads/tmp/ → expire after 7 days
rule 2 prefix originals/ → infrequent-access after 30 days
dry-run 142k objects match · 0 deleted now
Impact
−18 GB active · cost −$3.20/mo · fully reversible (rules only)

Proposal · Fix & replay 2 dead letters (order.paid)Ask a follow-upprp_qu20b9 · awaiting your review
Evidence — what I read
dlq 2 messages · both order.paid · since 14:03
cause TypeError: cannot read 'total' of null — "receipt":null in payload
correlation both from deploy #142 — receipt omitted for gift-card orders · retries 5/5 exhausted
Reasoning
The two dead letters share one root cause: deploy #142 emits order.paid without a receipt for gift-card orders, and the worker assumes one is present. This is a code fix, not a retry problem — replaying now would fail again. The fix is in deploy #143; once it ships, these two messages replay cleanly.
Proposed change
step 1 guard null receipt in worker — drafted, ships via deploy #143
step 2 after #143: replay 2 messages (idempotent — keyed by order_id)
step 3 add alert: DLQ depth > 0 (Alerts)
Impact
unblocks 2 paid orders · no retry-config change · replay is idempotent

Proposal · Switch eviction to allkeys-lru, raise maxmemoryAsk a follow-upprp_ca11e0 · awaiting your review
Evidence — what I read
memory used 1.9 GB of 2.0 GB (95%) · maxmemory-policy = noeviction
errors 3.1k OOM-command rejects/hr since 14:10 — writes failing, not evicting
keys hit rate 88% · session:* 61% · cart:* 22% · 40% of keys have no TTL
Reasoning
With noeviction and memory full, new writes are rejected (the OOM errors), not old keys dropped. session:* and cart:* are cache-safe to evict by LRU — the app treats a miss as a cold read. Raising maxmemory to 3 GB restores headroom; allkeys-lru ends the write failures.
Proposed change
- maxmemory-policy noeviction
+ maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
- maxmemory 2 GB
+ maxmemory 3 GB
Impact
write failures → 0 · hit rate ≈ unchanged · cost +$11/mo (2→3 GB)
Open in Settings (D14)Apply in staging firstDismiss (logged)Applied as you, via assistant — same permissions, same audit

Attached insight1 of 3 open ▾
Valkey eviction → allkeys-lru
prp_ca11e0 · cache · awaiting review
View
I've loaded this recommendation’s evidence and reasoning — ask anything about it.
Why allkeys-lru and not volatile-lru?
volatile-lru only evicts keys that have a TTL — but 40% of your keys (including some session:*) have none, so under pressure it can still hit OOM and reject writes. allkeys-lru can evict anything, which is what guarantees writes keep succeeding.
from the evidence40% keys · no TTL
If you'd rather keep eviction scoped, I can draft a TTL policy for session:* first — then volatile-lru becomes safe. Want that as an alternative proposal?
And if I lower maxmemory instead of raising it?
That trades cost for hit rate. At 1.5 GB you'd evict ~2× more often — hit rate drops from 88% toward ~80%, pushing more cold reads onto db-main (already your slow path). It saves ~$6/mo but adds downstream load.
Model both side by side

U5Interactions · drawer, async state — Add custom domain mid-verification: DNS records, live dig checks, “close this — we keep checking”; cert issues automatically. TLS never optional.
Add custom domain
api · ecommerce / production
✓Domain added2Verifying DNS3Cert issued
Domain
shop.acme.devverifying
Add these records at your DNS provider
CNAME shop api-x1lk3.steloit.app
TXT _steloit.shop verify=a91c4e22
Live checkevery 60 s
dig CNAME shop.acme.dev → not found yet
dig TXT _steloit.shop → ✓ verify=a91c4e22
You can close this. Checking continues in the background; the certificate issues and attaches automatically the moment DNS resolves (usually minutes, up to 48 h). You’ll get a bell when it’s live — and TLS is never optional (never gated, either).

PostgreSQL 16.4 · branches are copy-on-write — created in seconds, billed by delta
New branch
main production the live database · 21.4 GB · PITR 7 days degraded Open
staging env: staging refreshed nightly from main · 21.4 GB base + 218 MB delta $4.10/mo ready Open
preview/pr-142 preview env · PR #142 branched from main @ 13:52 · scoped credentials · auto-retires when PR closes $0.90/mo ready Open
restore-drill-jul restore verify restored from backup 06 Jul 03:00 · verification passed · retires in 20h $0.20 ready Open
Why branches
Every preview environment gets a real copy of production data in seconds, isolated and disposable. Restores are rehearsed the same way: restore into a branch, verify, promote — disaster recovery you can practice.
From the CLI
steloit db branch create fix-index --from main steloit db branch promote fix-index --to staging

Proposal · Add index to orders Ask a follow-upprp_7c31a2 · awaiting your review
Evidence — what I read
query SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = $1 ORDER BY created_at DESC
plan Seq Scan on orders (rows=1,204,318) · Sort · 642 ms avg since deploy #142
metrics calls 214/min (was 3/min) · 61% of db time · connections 96% of pool
Reasoning
Deploy #142 made this query hot on every gift-card page load. orders.customer_id has no index, so each call scans 1.2M rows, holding connections long enough to saturate the pool — the cause of the api latency alert.
Proposed migration — a draft, not an action
-- 0049_idx_orders_customer.sql
+ CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_orders_customer_created
+ ON orders (customer_id, created_at DESC);
Predicted: 642 ms → ~4 ms Index size: ~96 MB (+$0.02/mo) Build: non-blocking, ~3 min
Open in preview branch Apply to production… Dismiss (logged) Applied changes are audited as you, via assistant — same permissions, same confirmations.
The four laws, enforced here
AI proposes; you dispose — this card is a draft artifact.
Explained & auditable — evidence and reasoning shown above.
Reads broadly, writes narrowly — within your permissions only.
Optional — an org Policy can turn this panel off entirely.
Suggested path
1 · Apply in preview/pr-142 branch
2 · Verify plan flips to Index Scan
3 · Promote migration with deploy #143
Never proposed one-click: IAM, secrets, network exposure, deletions. Those the assistant only describes how to do.

Soft limits never break production. (AI Gateway tokens are infrastructure — metered like any resource, not a plan quota.) Egress, events, AI requests, builds and seats keep working past the line and meter as overage — the limit is a billing threshold, not a wall.
Hard limits fail loudly and early. Previews queue with a stated reason; the API returns 429 with Retry-After. You’re warned at 80% (B8) before either happens.

Warnings fire at 80% of any allowance — in the console, the bell, and email to Admins. Never after the fact.
The math, in the open
pace 87 GB in 21 days → ~4.1 GB/day → ~118 GB by Apr 1
overage ~18 GB × $0.09 = ~$1.62 on the April invoice
driver assets bucket · 71% of egress · spiked with the gift-card launch

Upgrade prompts here are calculators, not sales — the console recommends a plan only when the math favors you, and shows the math either way.

Billing · Cancel Pro
Borealis · effective at your anchor, Apr 5 · this page is the exit interview the honest way: what stops, what keeps running, what it takes to come back.
On Apr 5, Borealis moves to Free
Keeps running: your project, services, data, domains — and usage keeps billing at the same unit prices. Cancelling the plan is not deleting resources.
Winds down: preview environments (Free has none) close when their PRs do; log retention shortens to 3 days going forward — nothing already recorded is retro-deleted early.
Over Free limits: you’re at 2 members (limit 3) and 1 project (limit 1) — within limits, nothing blocks this cancellation. If you were over, this page would say exactly what to reduce, like the downgrade button does (B4).
Nothing is deleted. Not at cancellation, not after. Deletion is only ever yours to do — or the day-90 billing rule with final notice.
Why are you leaving? optional — one question, no follow-ups
Too expensiveMissing featuresProject endedOther
Cancel Pro — effective Apr 5Keep Pro
Coming back
Reactivation is one click, any time. Until Apr 5: “Resume Pro” simply uncancels — nothing was interrupted. After: “Restart Pro” re-bills $29 and every capability returns instantly — previews, retention, seats — because nothing was deleted in between.
Resume Pro (undo cancellation)
No retention offers, no guilt modals, no hidden “pause” tier. The way back is as clean as the way out — that asymmetry is what dark patterns break.

What “disable AI” doesLaw 4
Set ai-assistant to disabled and every AI surface disappears — the Assistant page, ⌘K “ask”, describe-to-provision (AI1), and the per-product panels.
